messages:
Samira (CS): FYI escalating a customer outage + billing noise. Customer reports repeated duplicate generations after an SSE disconnect + reconnect flow. They see partial output, then a reconnect that appears to re-run the remainder and bill twice. They provided a short repro and logs, putting it here so eng/runtime can triage. @Jonathan (eng-runtime) @Lee

Jonathan (eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the repro and the exact headers they sent? key things: resume token usage, idempotency headers, and whether the reconnect used the same session id.

Samira (CS): paste from customer (redacted):
--- customer repro steps ---
1) Start streaming request to our hosted endpoint (POST /v1/streams/generate) with streaming SSE response. Headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx, Content-Type: application/json. No Idempotency-Key on first start.
2) After ~1s they cut the TCP connection (simulating flaky mobile). Client reconnects and calls POST /v1/streams/reconnect with body: {"resume_token":"r_ABC123","model":"redwood-v1"} but they omitted Idempotency-Key header on reconnect.
3) On server side they see: first session created run_id=run_01, partial token stream ended at sequence 57. Reconnect created run_id=run_02 and produced tokens from 58..end again. Billing shows two generation records for run_01 and run_02.
--- logs (trimmed) ---
[ingest] recv start -> run_id=run_01 session=ses_42
[emit] sse chunk seq=55 data="..."
[emit] sse chunk seq=56 data="..."
[conn] tcp closed by client
[reconnect] incoming resume_token=r_ABC123 session=null idempotency=null -> created new run run_02 session=ses_43
[emit] sse chunk seq=58 data="..." (this chunk overlaps previous when assembled by client)

Customer claim: "we got duplicate tokens and were charged for another full generation. When we replayed with resume_token we expected resume semantics, not a fresh run"

Maya (support): adding context: customer is on Dedicated plan, expects resume semantics to be idempotent. They say their client followed the public reconnect guide we have (but may have missed Idempotency-Key). They attached a capture of SSE frames showing duplicated text fragments.

Lee (eng-ml): initial thought: sounds like server treats reconnect without an idempotency key as a new start instead of a resume when session not found. Resume should be decided by a combination of resume_token validity and/or explicit Idempotency-Key from the client. We probably have a race: session tombstone cleaned before reconnect arrives, and we create a new run rather than reattaching to existing cache.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): I dug into the logs — the reconnect path currently does: validate resume_token -> check active_session_by_token -> if not found, create new run and attempt to resume using kv-cache snapshot if available. But kv-cache lookup can return stale snapshot which causes overlaps. Also billing currently charges on run creation, not on final confirmation, so new run creation increments billing. That's our immediate problem.

Samira (CS): customer is asking for (A) explanation of duplicate billing and (B) mitigation so they don't get charged twice for the same logical generation. They need repro steps they can run to demonstrate and test fixes.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): quick mitigation ideas:
- Server-side: if reconnect carries the original run id OR a resume_token that maps to a recent tombstoned run (< X seconds), treat as same run and do not create a new billing entry. Delay tombstone GC for a longer tail to allow client reconnects.
- Billing: make generation_id dedupe by resume_token or initial_start_nonce when billing ingestion occurs — if a new run references the same resume_token and starts within N seconds, mark it as potential duplicate and hold charge until verification.
- Client guidance: always set Idempotency-Key on the initial start and send the same Idempotency-Key on reconnect; include resume_token in reconnect and prefer session_id if present.

Maya (support): can you propose a concrete repro that the customer can run and share command lines? They prefer curl/node snippets.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): repro snippet (SSE simulated):
```bash
# start streaming (client sets idempotency on start)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-foo" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 1111-2222" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```
Then kill connection after a few chunks (CTRL-C) and immediately reconnect:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-foo" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 1111-2222" \
  -d '{"resume_token":"r_ABC123","model":"redwood-v1"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/reconnect
```
This should cause the server to reattach rather than create a new generation if idempotency key + resume_token match.

Samira (CS): customer said they were not sending Idempotency-Key on start (oops) — they expected resume_token alone to be sufficient. Is that reasonable / documented? We need to update docs if we require Idempotency-Key.

Lee (eng-ml): resume_token alone should be sufficient in principle, but we need robust mapping from resume_token -> canonical_generation_id. If the resume_token encodes generation id (or is stored server-side mapping) then we can dedupe billing strictly on that. Right now token->run mapping is ephemeral and GC'd quickly.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): action plan I suggest: (short term) extend tombstone window to 60s for resume_tokens and add a best-effort mapping so reconnects within window reuse existing run_id (no additional billing). (mid term) persist resume_token -> run_id mapping in the metadata DB and make billing dedupe rely on that mapping. (long term) add server-side idempotency check on reconnect: if the incoming reconnect references a resume_token that maps to an in-progress or recently finished run, link rather than create.

Maya (support): can we implement the short-term change today? we have a customer on Dedicated, would be good to flip a config flag.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): I can push a toggle: increase tombstone GC to 60s and route reconnects to try reattach before creating a new run. I'll open a small PR and roll to staging. Need someone to approve.

ops-bot: deployment scheduled: runtime/resume-token-gc-toggle -> staging at 1719002800. Owner: jonathan.w

Maya (support): I'll tell customer to hold off on further retries and share the curl repro with Idempotency-Key. Also we'll ask billing to not finalize the charge while we investigate.

billing-bot: billing ticket created: BILL-9123 linking runs run_01/run_02. Owner: billing-team. Status: investigating potential duplicate charges. Reference: customer acct acct_777.

Lee (eng-ml): also note: client-side should avoid replaying partial output when reconnect causes overlaps. Recommend client assemble using sequence numbers from SSE frames (we attach seq=n to each chunk) and dedupe overlaps by seq. Example SSE fragment we send now:
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":56,"token":"hello","resume_token":"r_ABC123"}

```
Client should ensure it doesn't double-append if it sees seq <= last_confirmed_seq. If resume happens and server restarts from seq 56, client can drop duplicates up to seq 56 then append from 57.

Samira (CS): customer will run the curl repro with Idempotency-Key and confirm. If they still see duplicates we'll escalate for immediate mitigation. Also we need to update public docs that resume semantics are guaranteed only when either resume_token maps to an active run OR when Idempotency-Key is preserved across reconnect.

Jonathan (eng-runtime): summarizing next steps:
- Jonathan: open PR to extend resume_token tombstone (staging deploy scheduled) -> target: 1719002800.
- Jonathan: add quick billing guard to hold charges for new runs referencing recent resume_token for 24h while we verify.
- Lee: add client guidance snippet (seq dedupe) to docs.
- Maya/Samira: send templated repro + ask customer to run with Idempotency-Key and share logs.

Maya (support): thanks, I'm sending the template now to customer and will update this thread with their result.

Samira (CS): adding final note: customer impact low (one customer, Dedicated), but billing annoyance is sensitive. please prioritize the short-term GC toggle and billing hold. Thanks all. :pray:
